channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: Saudi ambassador compares the Houthis to ISIS, calls for a broad coalition
item.description: Saudi Arabia's ambassador to the US, Princess Reema bint Bandar Al Saud, compared the Houthis to ISIS in a New York Times op-ed published after a deadly attack on Riyadh's airport.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 1.1mn citizens returned from abroad in 9M26, 172,000 found permanent jobs
item.description: More than 1.1 million Uzbeks returned from abroad in January–September 2026. According to the Ministry of Employment, 172,000 found permanent jobs and 349,000 became self-employed, but 257,000 remain unemployed.

item.title: Israel's election ends without a majority; Germany reacts cautiously
item.description: In the October 27 Knesset election no bloc reached 61 seats; Netanyahu's bloc took 53 and the opposition 48. Germany is withholding judgment until a coalition is clear.

item.title: Uzbekistan's poverty rate fell from 5.8% to 3.6% in nine months — Employment Ministry
item.description: According to the Ministry of Employment and Poverty Reduction's nine-month 2026 results, the poverty rate fell from 5.8% to 3.6% and 824,000 people were placed in permanent jobs.

item.title: IISS: Gulf states must rethink their trillion-dollar defence after the war
item.description: According to the IISS Strategic Dossier "The Gulf at War," the 2026 war exposed the weakness of the Gulf states' US-weapons-reliant defence.

item.title: Uzbekistan sets up nuclear classes at two Tashkent academic lyceums — Uzatom
item.description: The Tashkent branch of the MEPhI nuclear university is opening specialised nuclear classes at the I. M. Gubkin and International House-Tashkent academic lyceums to prepare students for the country's nuclear energy sector.

item.title: Barack Obama campaigns in Georgia ahead of midterms and criticizes the Donald Trump administration
item.description: Five days before the US midterm elections, former president Barack Obama backed Democratic senator Jon Ossoff; he said the Trump administration mobilized a 'whole-of-government response' to a joke. Polls suggest Democrats could take the House.

item.title: France: Trappes shooting suspect admits he chose victims by religion and race
item.description: A gun attack on October 23, 2026 in Trappes and La Verrière near Paris killed one person and wounded seven. According to the anti-terrorism prosecutor, the 39-year-old suspect admitted deliberately targeting people who appeared Muslim or of African origin.

item.title: How International Sanctions Work: An Explainer
item.description: Sanctions are economic and political restrictions used by a state or group of states to achieve a goal. Here are their types, who imposes them, their financial mechanisms, and their impact on Central Asia.

item.title: US: five days to the midterms — Barack Obama rallies for Democrats in Georgia
item.description: On November 3 the entire House of Representatives and 35 Senate seats are up for election. Former president Barack Obama held a rally in Morrow, Georgia, backing Senator Jon Ossoff and gubernatorial nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms.

item.title: The establishment of diplomatic relations between Uzbekistan and China (1991–1996)
item.description: In its first years of independence, Uzbekistan and the People's Republic of China established formal relations: China's recognition of Uzbekistan's independence, the exact date of diplomatic relations, the embassies, Islam Karimov's first visit, and the founding documents, set out on the basis of sources.

item.title: Japan-built water system in Tajikistan ran only 10.9 hours a day — external review gave it the lowest 'D' rating
item.description: JICA's external evaluation gave the Khatlon water project the lowest possible rating: designed for 24-hour supply, service was limited by leaks and excessive use. Even so, Japan has signed a new grant for another district.

item.title: UNICEF study: in migrant families, one in three children takes on housework and sibling care
item.description: Of 702 children aged 11–17 surveyed in families where parents had left for labor migration in Uzbekistan, about a third took on duties parents used to perform; most stayed in school, but UNICEF recorded a decline in mood.

item.title: The Deportation of the Volga Germans to Central Asia (1941)
item.description: On 28 August 1941 a decree dissolved the Volga German Autonomous Republic and deported over half a million Germans to Kazakhstan, Siberia, the Altai and Central Asia — including Uzbekistan. A history of the deportation, the Labour Army, the special-settlement regime and rehabilitation.

item.title: Trappes attack suspect admits deliberately targeting Muslims and Africans — French prosecutor
item.description: The suspect in a shooting near Paris that killed one person had initially denied a racist motive; he now admits targeting people who appeared Muslim, African or North African, and that the attack was premeditated.

item.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 used real Itaewon disaster footage — families and gamers' association demand its removal
item.description: The opening cinematic of Activision's game used real news footage from the 2022 Itaewon crowd crush, in which 159 people died. Bereaved families demand a formal apology and that the clip be replaced.

item.title: How the US Electoral College Works
item.description: In the United States the president is not chosen by a direct popular vote but by a process called the Electoral College. Here is a clear, source-checked explainer of its 538 electors, the 270-vote threshold, the timeline, and the rules.

item.title: OSCE and Supreme Court train journalists in Termez on covering court proceedings
item.description: A two-day training in Termez taught journalists, bloggers and court press officers to report legal proceedings accurately while upholding the presumption of innocence.

item.title: Uzbekistan's membership in the international financial institutions (1992–1995): IMF, World Bank, EBRD and the Asian Development Bank
item.description: In its first years of independence, Uzbekistan joined the global financial system: the exact accession dates to the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank Group, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the Asian Development Bank, and their significance for economic integration.

item.title: Uzbekistan lets 2022/23 winter-intake master's students defend theses with a language certificate
item.description: Under a Higher Education Ministry commission decision, winter-intake master's students who could not defend their theses for lack of a foreign-language certificate may now do so on submitting a recognized certificate.

item.title: Egypt postpones stricter entry rules for Uzbek citizens until March 2027
item.description: After talks led by Uzbekistan's Foreign Ministry, Egypt delayed tighter Sinai entry rules until 1 March 2027; until then Uzbeks can visit Sharm el-Sheikh visa-free.

item.title: The Aral Sea Disaster: Why It Dried Up, Its Consequences, and Its Status Today
item.description: Once one of the largest inland bodies of water on Earth, the Aral Sea almost entirely disappeared within half a century. This is a factual explainer of the causes, consequences, and current restoration efforts.

item.title: US: Donald Trump escalates attacks on Abdul El-Sayed, a Muslim candidate for the Senate
item.description: If Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed wins, he would become the first Muslim US senator. President Donald Trump called him a "jihadist"; the candidate dismissed the remarks as a "distraction."

item.title: Migration and Urbanization in Turkestan under Tsarist Russia (1865–1917)
item.description: The flow of Russian settler colonists, the cotton economy, railways and the rise of new cities in Turkestan from the capture of Tashkent in 1865 to 1917.

item.title: Climatologist explains why air pollution rose in Central Asian cities in October
item.description: An institute analysis found that on 26 October the air quality index topped 100 in six of the region's eight major cities; climatologist Erkin Abdulakhatov explained the causes.

item.title: Thailand weighs 15-day visa-free entry for Uzbek citizens
item.description: Citing visa-processing delays, Thailand's Ministry of Tourism and Sports has proposed 15-day visa-free entry for citizens of Uzbekistan, Colombia and Mexico; the proposal goes to the Visa Policy Committee on 9 November.

item.title: How Life Insurance Works in the USA: A Guide for Immigrants
item.description: Life insurance is a contract with an insurer that pays a named beneficiary when the insured person dies. Here are its core concepts, types, cost factors, and US tax rules.

item.title: Uzbekistan introduces new benefits for doctors: mortgage help and remote-area allowances
item.description: At a meeting with medical and pharmaceutical workers, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced housing support, higher allowances for doctors in remote areas, and a drive to recruit Uzbek doctors with foreign clinical experience.

item.title: Uzbek citizens going abroad to study fall 33% in first nine months of 2026
item.description: According to the National Statistics Committee, 16,522 citizens left Uzbekistan for study in January–September 2026 — down a third year on year. Russia led the list while Tajikistan dropped from first place.

item.title: Uzbekistan summons Iranian ambassador over posts on Samarkand's heritage
item.description: The Foreign Ministry handed a note of protest to Iranian Ambassador Mohammad Ali Eskandari over social-media posts by Iranian diplomatic missions describing Samarkand's monuments as part of "Persian" or "Iranian-Islamic" civilization.
